key_insight: Perfumer uses an LLM-based agent to orchestrate faster first-principles workflows by combining learned structural pre-relaxation, Quantum ESPRESSO refinement, and electronic band prediction.
engineering_relevance: The framework could reduce computational cost and workflow setup effort when screening crystal structures and their electronic properties.
method: Translate natural-language requests into structure-to-band workflows.
Pre-relax structures with Perfumer-relax, then refine with Quantum ESPRESSO.
Predict 12 band energies at requested wavevectors using a periodic graph neural network and latent Hermitian spectral head that preserve reciprocal periodicity and time-reversal symmetry.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 2.75× overall relaxation speedup on tested structures; trained on 125,153 band structures, the band model achieves 0.157 eV median per-material MAE on 2,607 held-out-composition-family test materials and about 97 ms inference per material on two consumer CPU cores.
watch_item: The reported median band error does not establish worst-case accuracy or reliability for derived quantities such as band gaps; critical predictions warrant first-principles validation.
paper_title: Perfumer: A Large Language Model-based Agentic Framework Accelerating Structural Relaxation and Electronic Band Prediction for First-Principle Calculation
